items.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: It was a device of Ravel I suppose, but I’m talking about the pop songwriters

ctx.x: Exactly. Because of where it led the ear. And the minor seventh was a device of the pop song composers. It was a device of Ravel I suppose, but I’m talking about the pop songwriters like even the unschooled ones were using the minor seventh like Irving Berlin. The trained ones like Kern were using it too as part of their arsenal. It was the two chord, the minor seventh. That’s what changed jazz. That’s why jazz grew up the way it did. That’s my feeling.
